correctness.rationale: The q-factorial cyclotomic valuation is exactly the sum-of-residues floor deficit. Maximal residue sum is the greatest integer <= min(n,r(d-1)) in the residue class n mod d; a bounded-residue decomposition always attains it. For prime p the digit carry vectors satisfy the necessary-and-sufficient inequalities 0 <= n_j+p*c_(j+1)-c_j <= r(p-1). Coordinatewise maximum preserves the inequalities, including the crossing case, and digit sums reconstruct an actual r-composition, so all prime-power maxima coexist. Legendre and Phi_(p^j)(1)=p complete the specialization proof. Independent exact-integer tests ran 42310 compositions and 2610 q-factorizations. Quantifiers n>=1,r>=2; no inference to arbitrary q>=2.

originality.rationale: Guo 2009 proves precisely the two-part q-binomial polynomial LCM and its q=1 specialization; his Theorem 2 and Section 3 contain no r>=3 formula or closure of multi-carry vectors. Howard 1974 counts valuations of ordinary multinomials, sometimes by a full generating function; this may algorithmically imply the integer half, but not the q-polynomial factorization and its equality with ordinary LCM for every r. Bergman 2008 concerns common divisors/GCD rather than all-row LCM. Focused exact-title, parameter, implication and database searches found no stronger result covering the combined claim; non-indexed literature remains a real risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed or terminologically different literature may contain the same q-multinomial polynomial LCM formula.

value.rationale: The finding completely determines the natural LCM of r-part Gaussian multinomial rows for all n and r; unlike binary Guo, nontrivial cyclotomic multiplicities occur. It proves the nonautomatic specialization equality by an explicit lattice closure property of carry vectors. Polynomial LCMs generally do not commute with evaluation (for example Phi_2(q) and Phi_4(q) both evaluate to 2 at q=1, while their polynomial LCM evaluates to 4), so the compatibility has mathematical content. The integer formula can compute an exact modular-divisibility invariant without enumeration.
